# 1 Clement Chapter 51 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 51 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_051_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 51

**51:1** Whatever things we have transgressed, and whatever things we have done through the stratagems of the adversary, let us ask to be forgiven for them. And those who became leaders of revolt and sedition ought to look to the common hope.

**51:2** For those who conduct themselves in fear and love prefer to fall into distress themselves rather than let their neighbors suffer it — and they would rather have condemnation fall upon themselves than upon the harmony that has been handed down to us so nobly and righteously.

**51:3** For it is better for a man to confess his transgressions than to harden his heart, as the heart was hardened of those who raised rebellion against Moses the servant of God — whose judgment was made clear.

**51:4** For they went down into Hades alive, and "Death shall be their shepherd."

**51:5** Pharaoh and his army and all the rulers of Egypt, the chariots and their riders were swallowed up in the Red Sea and perished, for no other reason than that their foolish hearts were hardened after the signs and wonders had been performed in the land of Egypt through Moses the servant of God.

---

*LOGOS renders according to the standard Greek text of Codex Alexandrinus with attention to formal correspondence.*
